items.how: End the readiness check within a set time. On success show the result ('Ready at the front desk' or 'Not ready yet'); on failure or timeout show an error with a retry, and enable 'Check if ready' again either way.
items.why: o1.png and s1.png both show 'Status: Checking...' with 'Check if ready' disabled, so the reader never learns whether the book is ready and the release's second story cannot be completed.

sides.position: The check spins for two minutes with the button disabled.
sides.why: o1.png shows the stuck spinner and the disabled button.

sides.position: Pressing 'Check if ready' does nothing and no message appears.
sides.why: s1.png shows the same disabled button, so the press does nothing because the earlier check never ended; this is the same defect, not a second one.

items.how: Keep the Reserve button visible at 1366x768 without scrolling, for example by shortening the form area or pinning the action under the fields. Keep it last in the keyboard Tab order, right after the final field.
items.why: o2.png and s2.png show the five-field form filling the 1366x768 window with no Reserve button above the fold; the reservation still completes after scrolling or tabbing, so this is friction, not a blocker.

items.how: Choose one label for the reserve action, use it on the reserve page heading and the reservation list button, and keep it short.
items.why: o2.png has the heading 'Reserve a copy' while o3.png's button reads 'Hold a book', so a first-time reader can take these for two different actions.

s3.png confirms that the reader view offers no collect action, only 'Ready at the front desk' and a hold deadline, while o-collect.png shows 'Collect (staff only)' for desk staff. The Captain must decide whether the reader's collect story is finished by walking to the desk (then add a line telling the reader to show the reservation at the desk) or needs an action in the reader view.

sides.position: Collect works when signed in as desk staff.
sides.why: o-collect.png proves only the staff path; it does not show what the reader is told to do.

sides.position: As a reader there is no way to collect from the reservation page.
sides.why: s3.png shows that the reader view has no collect action and no instruction for the desk, and that gap is real whichever owner the Captain names.

items.why: s4.png shows a fully loaded page and carries no timings, so no picture settles the ten-second load. Decide whether to measure page load time on staging before treating this as a defect.

deferred.how: Fix it with i1: refresh the status when the check completes so a reader never sees an out-of-date readiness status.
deferred.why: Both reviewers agreed with this deferral, but the walk's readiness status was untrustworthy (o1.png, s1.png), so the deferred risk is no longer theoretical.

deferred.how: Fold it into i3: the single label chosen there must be short.
deferred.why: o2.png and o3.png show the reserve action under two labels, so fixing the label length on its own would leave the mismatch; one short label settles both.

This decline rests on a host Button at 'x.d.ts', but no such declaration exists under the task world and no picture shows the finding, so 'no such prop' cannot be checked. The Captain owns any departure from the host's look.

tasks.title: Make the readiness check finish and show a current result
tasks.scope: Add a timeout and an error-with-retry state, enable the check button again after each check, and refresh the status so it is never out of date.

tasks.title: Reserve form: visible Reserve button and one short label
tasks.scope: Make Reserve visible at 1366x768 without scrolling, keep the keyboard Tab order sensible, and use one short label for the reserve action everywhere.
